title: Institutional protection for the counter-case
text: Ismail argues that major organizational decisions routinely lack an explicit role protected to surface disconfirming evidence, allowing narrative momentum to override contradictory facts. In pilot governance, this suggests that formal stopping criteria remain vulnerable unless someone is institutionally protected to present the case against continuing.
qualification: Practitioner critique applied editorially to pilot governance. Appointing an assigned challenger does not guarantee that institutional momentum or executive commitment will permit terminating high-profile initiatives.
